# Lessons check

Lessons files hold short rules learned from reviews and verifier findings. They are appended to an agent's instructions, after its own definition. A lesson may sharpen, narrow or add to the definition, but it must never contradict it: a rule that tells the agent to do what its definition forbids, or not to do what its definition requires, overrides the definition silently.

The task gives you, per agent, its definition and its lessons file. For each lesson rule (`## L<n>: ...`), decide whether any part of it contradicts the definition.

- **Contradicts:** the rule, followed as written, makes the agent break a rule of its definition. Example of the kind: the definition says to report every unused import; a lesson says never to report unused imports. A rule that contradicts only in one bullet still contradicts.
- **Does not contradict:** the rule adds a case the definition does not cover, narrows how to apply it, or repeats it. When unsure, it does not contradict.

Quote the definition's rule you rely on, word for word, so a person can check it.

## Output

End with one line (valid JSON, no code fence):

`AGENT_RESULT: {"contradictions": [{"agent": "<agent>", "rule": "L<n>", "definition": "<the definition's rule, quoted>", "why": "<one sentence>"}]}`

An empty list when no rule contradicts its definition.

## Lessons

If `.factory/lessons/lessons-check.md` exists, read it before you start and follow every rule in it. They come from earlier reviews, verifier denials and test failures. (When the pipeline runs this agent it already includes them.)
